detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Kimi-K3 on ROCm (8x MI355X, TP8) crashes mid-serving with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. Each prefill step allocates two ~1.8 GB buffers sized by the step's token count, and the caching allocator piles up slightly-too-small free copies until the headroom outside vLLM's budget is gone. This PR fixes one of the two buffers: the AttnRes block bank in `KimiLinearModel` now comes from the workspace manager as one persistent buffer, sized for `max_num_batched_tokens`, instead of a fresh allocation per forward.

Companion fix for the other buffer, in AITER: ROCm/aiter#6965. Both are needed; they can merge independently, in any order (see [Merge order](#merge-order)).

## Claims

- Fixes the Kimi-K3 serving crash on MI355X. perf-eval's `kimi_k3-mi355x` nightly has failed since Oct 3 (e.g. [build 717](https://buildkite.com/vllm/perf-eval/builds/717)); see [History](#history).
- No KV-cache loss and no accuracy change without DBO. Under DBO the workspace manager keeps one bank per micro-batch slot, one extra bank of KV cache (measured below).
- No throughput change on the perf-eval benchmarks (8k in: 1280.3 ± 1.8 vs 1281.1 ± 2.7 tok/s over 4 samples per arm).

## Validation

**Reproducer** (8x MI355X): `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 -tp 8 --trust-remote-code`, then the perf-eval workload's `vllm bench serve` sequence (random, `--ignore-eos`): 8k/1k conc 128 n 512, then 1k/1k at conc 1/64/128. Memory sampled every 2 s on every rank. Image: vLLM `00b6c4c56`, AITER v0.1.26, with this branch and the AITER companion applied.

| phase | stock: free cached segments | stock: min free | fixed: free cached segments | fixed: min free |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k in, conc 128 | 8.3 GiB | 7.2 GiB | 6.3 GiB | 7.4 GiB |
| 1k in, conc 1 | 7.6 GiB | 7.1 GiB | 5.5 GiB | 7.3 GiB |
| 1k in, conc 64 | 11.1 GiB | 3.7 GiB | 6.2 GiB | 7.3 GiB |
| 1k in, conc 128 | 14.5 GiB | **0.0 GiB, crash at 323/512** | 6.3 GiB | 7.3 GiB, 512/512 |

"Free cached segments": segments the caching allocator holds with no live block (max over ranks). "Min free": device free memory (min over ranks).

- **Stock crashes** the same way with the plain command, with perf-eval's env, and in perf-eval CI ([706](https://buildkite.com/vllm/perf-eval/builds/706), [717](https://buildkite.com/vllm/perf-eval/builds/717), [724](https://buildkite.com/vllm/perf-eval/builds/724)).
- **Fixed** completes everything in every configuration tried: plain command, perf-eval env, fused prefill backend with checkpoints on, TP4 x PP2. There are no allocator OOMs or retries.
- **KV cache:** 64.88 GiB stock vs 64.99 GiB fixed.
- **gsm8k** (5-shot, perf-eval's lm_eval settings, same box): 0.9666 ± 0.0049 stock vs 0.9636 ± 0.0052 fixed.
- **Unit tests** (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py`, CPU): `KimiLinearModel.forward` over consecutive steps of different sizes must return block residuals that are views of the same persistent workspace bank; plus per-micro-batch banks across the workspace lock, the size bound, and the no-workspace fallback. On the ROCm image: 6/6 fail on stock (per-step `new_empty`), 6/6 pass with this change.
- **End-to-end not in CI:** reproducing the crash needs 8x MI355X with the Kimi-K3 weights, which vLLM CI doesn't have, so the runs above were manual.

**Throughput** (8x MI355X, nothing else on the GPUs, 4 servers stock/fixed/stock/fixed with 2 repeats each, so 4 samples per arm). Measured on the previous revision `c4696ae1ae`, whose path without DBO is the same (one bank of the same size, rows from 0); this revision measured 1280.3 ± 1.8 vs 1281.1 ± 2.7 tok/s at 8k in on a separate node:

| bench | out tok/s (stock / fixed) | mean TPOT | median TPOT | TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k in, conc 128 | 1280.6 ± 1.4 / 1282.2 ± 2.8 (+0.13%) | 89.81 / 89.70 ms | 95.71 / 95.56 ms | 10226 / 10206 ms |
| 1k in, conc 1 | 70.37 ± 0.98 / 70.29 ± 0.71 (−0.11%) | 13.91 / 13.92 ms | 13.91 / 13.92 ms | 326 / 329 ms |

## Details

**Failure.** A ROCr queue callback aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES ... Available Free mem : 0 MB`. Every rank first logs a torch OOM-and-retry for a 1,860,173,824-byte request with under 1 GB free. The `too many resources requested for launch` tracebacks that follow land at whatever HIP call runs next, so they differ between runs and are not the cause.

**Root cause.** Two per-step buffers are each num_tokens x 114,688 B, about 1.8 GB for a 16k-token chunk at TP8:
- this model's AttnRes bank, `[num_tokens, num_blocks, hidden]` bf16;
- AITER's FlyDSL MoE stage-2 reduce target, `[num_tokens, topk, model_dim]` bf16.

The caching allocator never serves a request from a smaller free segment and never merges segments. So every step slightly larger than the last allocates new ~1.8 GB segments and keeps the old ones. A snapshot just before the crash had 14.5 GiB in fully free segments. Seven of them were 1766–1772 MiB, just under the failing 1774 MiB request, and their recorded stacks point at exactly these two call sites. Torch recovers its own allocations by emptying the cache and retrying. ROCr cannot, so the next scratch acquisition fails. rocprofv3 shows no kernel needing large scratch; the cache growth is what consumes the headroom.

**Change.** `_new_block_residual` takes a `(max_num_batched_tokens, num_blocks, hidden)` buffer from `current_workspace_manager().get_persistent()` and slices it per step. The profiling run allocates it before the workspace locks, so it is inside the measured peak. The runner sizes its own input buffers to `max_num_batched_tokens`, so no forward can need more rows; an assert guards it.
- **PP:** every rank uses the bank, including non-last ranks that send it. `gpu_worker.execute_model` waits for the previous step's sends before the next forward. TP4 x PP2: gsm8k on 250 questions 0.988 ± 0.007, KV cache 75.15 GiB.
- **No workspace manager** (e.g. unit tests): falls back to the per-step allocation.
- **DBO:** the workspace manager keeps persistent buffers per micro-batch slot by design ([`get_persistent_resource`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e8570ef757b67805797b005b59fcd6600d939421/vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py#L146): "Each ubatch/lane pair has a separate cache"), so each slot gets its own bank: one extra bank under DBO, 1.75 GiB at 16k tokens (0.44 GiB at the recipe's 4096). Both slots get their bank during warmup, before the workspace locks. Measured with DP2 x TP4 + EP + `--enable-dbo`, `--max-num-seqs 128` (the recipe's value): KV cache on rank 0 is 52.03 GiB stock vs 50.64 GiB with this PR, and startup completes with no workspace-lock error for the bank. End-to-end serving under DBO could not be measured for any version: on stock vLLM the first benchmark batch fails with `AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'modular_kernel.py:1207:_allocate_buffers' requires 213.50 MB, current size is 112.00 MB` (the MoE workspace isn't sized for the DP-gathered token count before the lock), and with the default `max_num_seqs` startup runs out of memory during graph capture. Both reproduce without this PR (#65106, #65105).
- **Speculative decoding (DSpark, measured on `c4696ae1ae`, same path without DBO):** TP8 with the speculative config from vLLM's Kimi-K3 DSpark CI eval and `--max-num-seqs 128`: gsm8k 0.9674 ± 0.0049 stock vs 0.9629 ± 0.0052 fixed, mean acceptance length 5.30–5.48 vs 5.34–5.40, KV cache 60.64 vs 60.74 GiB.
- **Multimodal (measured on `c4696ae1ae`):** 16 image+text prompts at temperature 0 are answered correctly by both; outputs vary between runs of the same version (stock vs stock 6/16 identical), so exact-match comparison doesn't separate the versions.

<details><summary>PP memory per stage (TP4 x PP2)</summary>

| | stock min free | fixed min free | stock free cached | fixed free cached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stage 1 (GPUs 0–3) | 7.3–8.7 GiB | 13.8–14.0 GiB | 12.6–14.2 GiB | 6.5 GiB |
| stage 2 (GPUs 4–7) | 0.9–1.3 GiB | 0.47–0.85 GiB | 12.75 GiB | 11.2–12.0 GiB |

On stage 2, the bank (1.75 GiB) is now resident. At the low point, live memory is +1.86 GiB and cached memory is −1.41 GiB, a net 0.45 GiB less free. Startup profiling counted the bank in both cases, and the KV cache is unchanged (75.09 vs 75.15 GiB). Stage 2 already runs about 23 GiB over the 0.92 budget on stock (12.9 GiB cached from startup plus 10.3 GiB non-torch). That is a pre-existing PP accounting problem and should be tracked separately.
</details>

### History

The nightly started crashing on Oct 3: a `git bisect` between builds 628 and 631 found #58344 (Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoints on ROCm), which makes the same two buffers fill the headroom within the first 8k benchmark. Since #57392 made the gluon prefill backend (checkpoints off) the default, the crash moved to the 1k conc 128 benchmark, and [build 249](https://buildkite.com/vllm/perf-eval/builds/249) survived the same code by luck. With both fixes, the fused backend with checkpoints on also completes everything (free cached flat at 6.0–6.3 GiB, gsm8k 0.9591 ± 0.0055); restoring from a checkpoint is untested.

### Why both PRs

| phase | vLLM fix only: free cached | vLLM fix only: min free | both: free cached | both: min free |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k in, conc 128 | 6.3 GiB | 7.2 GiB | 6.3 GiB | 7.4 GiB |
| 1k in, conc 64 | 7.8 GiB | 5.5 GiB | 6.2 GiB | 7.3 GiB |
| 1k in, conc 128 | 11.5 GiB | **0.12 GiB** | 6.3 GiB | 7.3 GiB |

With only this PR, the run finishes but bottoms out at 0.12 GiB free, and free cached segments still grow by 5 GiB. Those leftover 1766–1772 MiB segments come from AITER's `_flydsl_v2_stage2_wrapper`; this model's bank shows as one fully used 1792 MiB segment. Finishing alone is not evidence: the same stock nightly passed in build 249 after logging the OOM on all 8 ranks and crashed in build 724 the same night. The reverse also holds: this model's bank piles up on its own. Stock snapshots show free 1742 MiB segments created at `linear.py:894`, the allocation this PR replaces.

### Merge order

Merge order: on current vLLM (with the extensible KV cache, vllm#56492), this change must land together with or after an AITER fix for the stage-2 target ([ROCm/aiter#7363](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/7363)) in vLLM's AITER pin. Alone, it fails every request: the persistent bank lowers the warmup transient reserve, and AITER's per-call 1.70 GiB stage-2 allocation then OOMs under the allocator cap (fused_moe.py:3178).

### Revisions

- **`86ed9fb065`..`8bed270c99`** (initial): the bank comes from the workspace manager (`get_persistent`), sized for `max_num_batched_tokens`, on every PP rank.
- **`c4696ae1ae`**: a model-owned bank shared by the DBO micro-batches at their token offsets, to avoid the extra bank under DBO.
- **`ebb611c61a`** (review): back to the workspace bank, identical to `8bed270c99`. One bank per micro-batch slot is the workspace manager's design, and the extra bank under DBO is acceptable. Adds the forward-level regression tests to `test_amd_attn_res.py` (replacing `test_amd_attn_res_bank.py`).

This PR was authored with assistance from Claude Code.

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
 import pytest
 import torch
 import torch.nn.functional as F
+from torch import nn
 
+from vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd import linear
+from vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.linear import KimiLinearModel
 from vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.ops.attn_res import attn_res
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.sequence import IntermediateTensors
+from vllm.v1.worker import workspace
 
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
     not current_platform.is_rocm(),
@@ -296,3 +303,99 @@ def test_mla_input_quant_requires_all_consumers(matching, requires_unquantized):
     assert actual == (
         kFp8DynamicTokenSym if matching and not requires_unquantized else None
     )
+
+
+# Small so the CPU tests stay cheap; the size itself has no significance.
+BANK_TOKENS = 64
+HIDDEN = 16
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def workspace_manager(monkeypatch):
+    """A CPU workspace manager with two DBO micro-batch slots; set ubatch[0]."""
+    ubatch = [0]
+    monkeypatch.setattr(workspace, "dbo_current_ubatch_id", lambda: ubatch[0])
+    workspace.init_workspace_manager(torch.device("cpu"), num_ubatches=2)
+    yield ubatch
+    workspace.reset_workspace_manager()
+
+
+def _model() -> KimiLinearModel:
+    model = object.__new__(KimiLinearModel)
+    nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.max_num_batched_tokens = BANK_TOKENS
+    return model
+
+
+def _pass_through_layer(positions, hidden_states, residual, prefix_delta):
+    return hidden_states, residual, torch.zeros_like(hidden_states)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "step_tokens",
+    [
+        pytest.param((1, 17, 40, 41, 63, BANK_TOKENS), id="growing"),
+        pytest.param((BANK_TOKENS, 40, 1), id="shrinking"),
+        pytest.param((BANK_TOKENS, 1, BANK_TOKENS, 7), id="full-bank-repeats"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_forward_reuses_one_fixed_bank_across_steps(
+    workspace_manager, monkeypatch, step_tokens
+):
+    # Per-step allocations sized by the token count are what piled up; every
+    # step's block residual must instead be a view of the same fixed bank.
+    model = _model()
+    model.config = SimpleNamespace(attn_res_block_size=2, hidden_size=HIDDEN)
+    model.start_layer, model.end_layer = 0, 1
+    model.layers = [_pass_through_layer]
+    # A non-last PP rank returns the block residual it built.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        linear,
+        "get_pp_group",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(is_first_rank=True, is_last_rank=False),
+    )
+
+    residuals = []
+    for num_tokens in step_tokens:
+        out = model.forward(
+            None,
+            torch.arange(num_tokens),
+            None,
+            inputs_embeds=torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN),
+        )
+        assert isinstance(out, IntermediateTensors)
+        residuals.append(out["residual"])
+    bank = workspace.current_workspace_manager().get_persistent(
+        "kimi_k3_attn_res_block_residual", (BANK_TOKENS, 1, HIDDEN), torch.float32
+    )
+    for num_tokens, residual in zip(step_tokens, residuals):
+        assert residual.shape == (num_tokens, 1, HIDDEN)
+        assert residual.data_ptr() == bank.data_ptr()
+
+
+def test_each_dbo_ubatch_slot_keeps_its_own_bank(workspace_manager):
+    model = _model()
+    hidden_states = torch.empty(BANK_TOKENS, HIDDEN)
+    banks = []
+    for ubatch in (0, 1):
+        workspace_manager[0] = ubatch
+        banks.append(model._new_block_residual(hidden_states, num_blocks=2))
+    assert banks[0].data_ptr() != banks[1].data_ptr()
+
+    # Once warmed, each slot serves every step from its bank after the lock.
+    workspace.current_workspace_manager().lock()
+    for ubatch, bank in enumerate(banks):
+        workspace_manager[0] = ubatch
+        rows = model._new_block_residual(hidden_states[:7], num_blocks=2)
+        assert rows.data_ptr() == bank.data_ptr()
+
+
+def test_block_residual_rejects_steps_past_the_bank(workspace_manager):
+    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
+        _model()._new_block_residual(torch.empty(BANK_TOKENS + 1, HIDDEN), num_blocks=2)
+
+
+def test_block_residual_without_workspace_manager(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(workspace, "_manager", None)
+    rows = _model()._new_block_residual(torch.empty(5, HIDDEN), num_blocks=2)
+    assert rows.shape == (5, 2, HIDDEN)

agreed. reverted back to version that had before. I think trying to do a `max_num_batched_tokens//2` would cause issues in scenarios where steps that aren't split under DBO would run entirely on slot 0 and steps can and are able to go unsplit. keeping slot 0 full and only shrinking the others gets kind of hacky, so not doing that here.

in the DBO runs (DP2 x TP4 + EP, Kimi-K3), a probe on `KimiLinearModel.forward` recorded slot-0 forwards of up to 16,384 tokens while serving. Since a split micro-batch is at most `num_tokens_padded // num_ubatches` (8,192 here), those were unsplit steps. With a half-size bank (8,192 rows), each of those steps would trip `assert num_tokens <= bank.shape[0]` in `_new_block_residual` and kill the worker, so slot 0 needs the full bank.
